texts.preamble: Page No.# 1/8 vs The State Of Assam on 7 August, 2025 Page No.# 1/8 Gahc010219822012 2025:Gau-As:11337 The Gauhati High Court (High Court Of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram And Arunachal Pradesh) Case No. : Crl.Rev.P./519/2012 Md. Tayez Ali S/O- Zodib Ali, R/O- No. 2 Darokanagar, P.O.- Khagrabari, P.S.- Dhaligaon, Dist.- Chirang, Btad, Assam. Versus The State Of Assam
texts.facts: 2. The revision petitioner, namely, Md. Tayez Ali, has filed this petition aggrieved by the concurrent decisions of the learned courts Page No.# 2/8 below convicting and sentencing him under Section 7 r/w Section 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein PFA Act). 3. The case was initiated based on a complaint dated 07.11.2008 by the Senior Food Inspector, Bongaigaon, during normal checking and the present petitioner, who was a milk vendor, was Page No.# 1/8 vs The State Of Assam on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173286470/ 1 checked with regard to the milk that he was stated to be selling at Chapaguri, Bongaigaon. The sample sent to the public analyst also returned an adverse finding, stating that the milk was deficient in milk fat and solids, not fat as per standards prescribed in Appendix B of the PFA Act and Rules and hence, was adulterated as per the same law. 4. The complaint resulted in the prosecution of the revision petitioner and during the trial, the Senior Food Inspector and one peon working in the office of Joint Director of Health Services, Bongaigaon were examined as prosecution witnesses, being PW-1 and PW-2, both of whom were cross-examined. Various documents were exhibited by the prosecution. Accordingly, the convicted appellant is Page No.# 3/8 before this Court with the revision.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the petitioner who based his submissions mainly on two contentions/points- No. (i) that before taking the sample of milk, there was no stirring of the same on the part of the senior food inspector; (ii), that the sample was sent to the public analyst after three days instead of the stipulated two days as required by Rule 18 of the PFA Rules. The aforesaid Rule 18 of the PFA Rules 1954, may be reproduced herein below- "18. Memorandum and impression of seal to be sent separately- A copy of the memorandum and specimen impression of the seal used to seal the packet shall be sent, in a sealed packet separately to the Public Analyst by any suitable means immediately but not later than the succeeding working days." 6. In support of his contentions, the learned counsel for the petitioner has placed before this court a judgment of this court rendered in the case of Jitendra Lal Gope vs. State of Tripura, reported in (2011) 2 GLR 829. In the said judgment, this Court referred to two decisions relied upon by the learned counsel in that case being Food Inspector, Municipal Corporation, Baroda vs. Madanlal Ramlal Sharma & Anr., reported in (1983) Crl. LJ 337 and State of Haryana vs. Daya Nand, reported in AIR (2004) SC 4358. 7. In para 7 of Madanlal Ramlal Sharma (supra), the Court Page No.# 4/8 reproduced para 8 of Daya Nath (supra), in which the Honorable Supreme Court held as- Our attention was not drawn to any provision in the Act or the Rules making it obligatory that churning should be done with some machine so as to make a sample homogeneous and representative sample. For this purpose churning is one of the methods of making the sample homogeneous and representative. 8. In para. 8 of the judgment also of Jitendra Lal Gope (supra) this court held that in the case of Daya Nand (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court reiterated that stirring of milk before taking sample is mandatory. In para 8 of Madanlal Ramlal Sharma(supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that there is no provision in the PFA act other rules which require stirring of the milk before taking a sample. However, it ensures that the food in question, that is the milk would be a homogeneous mixture from which a proper sample can be taken. In that judgment, the Hon'ble Apex Court also held that there is no particular manner by which such stirring is necessary. As already stated above, the para 8 of Jitendra Lal Gope (supra), this court has held after referring to Daya Nand (supra) that in case of milk stirring is necessary.
